4.text: On the first day the “fortifier” only supplies each of the inmates with a

5.text: new amulet, which is usually made of a scrap of sinew, and must be wrapped

6.text: either around the little finger of the right hand, or around the right wrist.

7.text: The ceremony begins with the dressing of the body in the funeral clothes,

8.text: which, for the most part, are prepared beforehand, especially by the older

9.text: people. Or at least the skins for that use have been stored in the clothing-

10.text: bags. Then all the women of the family take to cutting and preparing the

11.text: clothes with the utmost possible speed. New, unused clothes from the common

12.text: stores of the family may be employed for the funeral dress; but to leave the

13.text: body in its former every-day clothes is considered a slight to the deceased,

14.text: and is done only in the case of very poor people, or under extraordinary

15.text: circumstances; for instance, when death happens while on a journey in a

17.text: For male dress, no overcoat is used. For the dress of women, the old

18.text: overcoat of every-day wear may be used, but all tassels and fringes must be

19.text: taken off. No woven stuff bought from civilized people may form any part

20.text: of the funeral dress. In selecting skins for the funeral dress, preference is

21.text: given to the white ones, both for men and for women. The soles of the boots

22.text: must be of ground-seal skin, but not from the rough skin of the reindeer’s foot,¹

23.text: because the latter is not fit to wander in the regions of the deceased. The

24.text: cap forms no part of the funeral dress. In the dress of the women, the head

25.text: is covered with the hood of the overcoat; in the dress of the men, an extra

26.text: hood is sewed on to the fur shirt, contrary to the ordinary cut of this garment

27.text: among the Chukchee, but resembling the style of the Koryak. The Chukchee,

28.text: on the other hand, fashion this hood after the style of an infant’s garment,

29.text: which is also supplied with a large hood,¹ and they sometimes call a deceased

30.text: man “one with a hood.” This name is also applied to infants. The garments,

31.text: for the most part, are double, but not necessarily so. The stockings and the

33.text: The skins for the funeral dress must not be dyed with alder, which

34.text: calls to mind the proscription against the use of alder at the time of the

35.text: hunt of various animals.² The garments must be sewed with unblackened

36.text: sinew-thread, whereas the thread for the garments of the living must be

37.text: blackened with soot. No knots must be tied in the thread, as every knot

38.text: tied forebodes danger to the life of some member of the family.³ The funeral
